source.title: What Do Neural Networks Learn When Trained With Random Labels?
source.authors: Hartmut Maennel; Ibrahim M. Alabdulmohsin; I. Tolstikhin; R. Baldock; O. Bousquet; S. Gelly; Daniel Keysers

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, appendices, and figure captions are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on random labels and reports training-accuracy curves, but its experiments focus on downstream transfer and parameter alignment rather than directly reproducing the original random-label fitting and test-error comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training curves for random-label tasks, including downstream training from scratch and after random-label pre-training. Exact curve values are available only in figures. Cited results from other work were not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own SGD training-accuracy curves on entirely random labels, including models trained from scratch. These directly bear on V1 using the original method and measure, although the paper's main question concerns transfer. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve endpoints, so zero or near-zero training error cannot be verified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish covariance alignment analytically under stated assumptions and experimentally connect it to positive transfer. They attribute some negative transfer to later-layer specialization and persistent inactive ReLUs. Weight rescaling controls apply to Simple CNN and VGG16; ResNet18 is not rescaled, leaving a possible effective-learning-rate contribution.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses random-label pre-training followed by fine-tuning on disjoint data to investigate transfer and parameter alignment; it does not reproduce the original fitting and generalization comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer outcome varies with architecture, initialization scale, upstream class count and duration, number of transferred layers, dataset, and width; the authors report both positive and negative transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label training aligns first-layer parameter covariance with input covariance, with analytical and experimental evidence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained on random labels can learn second-order structure of the input distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label pre-training often accelerates downstream fitting; initialization, architecture and later-layer specialization can also produce negative transfer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label pre-training can help or hinder learning on disjoint downstream data, depending on the setting.

record.problems: Random-label fitting outcomes relevant to V1 appear in training-accuracy plots without exact reported values; the study's central comparisons concern transfer speed, not test error at chance for models fit to random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No exact random-label fitting rows could be extracted from the figures: the relevant training-accuracy curves are plotted without accompanying text or tables that state the outcomes numerically.

untested.parts: Random-label test accuracy versus chance is not reported. Zero or near-zero training error cannot be established from the supplied figure text. Matched true-label versus random-label fitting endpoints are not stated numerically.

No reported time-to-convergence ratio establishes a small constant-factor cost relative to true labels, and no corruption-fraction sweep tests progressive slowing. Faster downstream training after pre-training measures a different comparison.

Appendix E.1 trains fully connected networks on Gaussian inputs until convergence but does not establish zero training error. Shuffled-pixel and independently permuted-pixel fitting are not tested; patch permutation in Appendix E.2 measures parameter statistics.
No sweep from clean to fully corrupted labels jointly measures perfect training fit and steadily degrading test accuracy.
All experiments omit augmentation, weight decay and dropout. There is no comparison testing whether these prevent random-label fitting or whether removing them worsens true-label generalization.
The study does not measure shared real-label patterns being learned before noisy labels within training. Alignment and layer specialization do not establish that temporal ordering.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to repair. Random-label fitting curves are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed again as missing. Figure axes and captions alone do not establish curve endpoints; neither support nor failure of near-perfect fitting should be inferred from them. No verdict is assigned without readable fitting outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: The paper's random-label training curves bear on fitting, but do not report exact training-error values in text or tables; the direct random-label test error versus chance comparison and the same-network true-label generalization comparison are not tested here.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
